content.text: : infect of endocardium that typically affects 1+ valves
: male, >60yo, IVDU, poor dentition, struct Hdz (ex, MVP,
rheumatic Hdz), congenital Hdz (ex, bicuspid AV, VSD,
PDA), prior IE, indwelling IV, chronic hemodialysis, HIV⊕
▪︎rapid, fulminant progression; fatal w.in 6wks if left untx
▪︎S. aureus: acute clin course; common in IVDU	▪︎
▪︎Strep gallolyticus (formerly S. bovis): assoc w/ GI malignancy, CRC/IBD
▪︎malaise, HA, myalgia/arthralgia, night sweats, abd pain, dyspnea
▪︎also AMS, axial spine pain (osteomyelitis), PNA (septic pulm emboli)
(new/Δ), HF, arrhythmias (sus perivalvular abscess if new conduction delay)
▪︎septic emboli in 25%: septic pulm emboli, kidney + spleen infarct
▪︎splinter hemorrhages: nonblanching, linear, reddish-brown under nail bed
erythematous macules on palms/soles (cutaneous septic emboli)
nodules on finger/toe pads caused by immune complex deposition (“Osler, ouch”)
: round retinal hemorrhages w/ pale centers
▪︎Roth spots: also exudative, edematous, hemorrhagic; Janeway/Osler/Roth = less common but highly suggestive
(visual loss, motor weakness, aphasia), intracerebral hemorrhage, abscess
▪︎mnemonic FROM JANE: Fever, Roth spots, Osler nodes, Murmur, Janeway lesions, Anemia, Nailbed hemorrhages, Emboli
blood cultures x3 from separate sites
: vegetations (hyperechoic), perivalvular abscess, new valvular regurg, prosthetic valve dehiscence (rocking)
TTE w.in 12h of presentation, repeat after TX completed
➀ microorganisms shown by cx/histo of vegetation
➁ features of active endocarditis present on histo

➀ ⊕blood cx: typical organisms from 2 separate cx (S. aureus; viridans strep; S. gallolyticus incl nutritionally variant [Granulicatella, Abiotrophia]; HACEK; community-acquired enterococci w/o 1° focus) or persistently ⊕ (typical: ≥2 drawn >12h apart; skin contaminants: 3 or majority of ≥4 cx, first + last ≥1h apart) or single ⊕ Coxiella burnetii / phase I IgG >1:800
➁ endocardial involvement: echo ⊕ (vegetation, abscess, new partial dehiscence of prosthetic valve) or new valvular regurg (⇡ or Δ preexisting murmur alone ⍉sufficient)

predisposition (IVDU or predisposing heart condition); fever ≥38.0°C; vascular (major arterial emboli, septic pulm infarcts, mycotic aneurysm, ICH, conjunctival hemorrhages, Janeway lesions); immunologic (GN, Osler nodes, Roth spots, RF); microbiologic (⊕cx not meeting major criteria, or serologic evidence)
▪︎IE Sx resolve in ≤4d of ABX therapy
▪︎⍉pathologic evidence of IE found @ surg or autopsy after ≤4d ABX
: leukocytosis w/ Lt shift, ⇡ ESR/CRP, ⊕RF, anemia
: PVE, HF, uncontrolled IE, perivalvular ext/comp, fungal IE, ↑embolic risk
➀ presence of prosthetic valve or material
➃ repaired CHD during first 6mo after repair
➄ repaired CHD w/ residual defects
